claims.text: Changes in QRS axis or width are key signs of TCA toxicity.
claims.quote: Changes in the electrocardiogram, particularly in, QRS axis or width, are clinically significant indicators of tricyclic antidepressant toxicity.

claims.text: A rightward axis shift of the terminal QRS, with a prolonged QT and sinus tachycardia, is a specific and sensitive sign of first-generation TCA overdose.
claims.quote: a rightward axis shift in the terminal QRS complex together with a prolonged QT interval and sinus tachycardia are specific and sensitive indicators of first generation tricyclic overdose.

claims.text: Their absence does not exclude overdose.
claims.quote: The absence of these findings is not exclusionary.

claims.text: A maximal limb-lead QRS of ≥0.10 seconds may best indicate how severe the overdose is.
claims.quote: A maximal limb-lead QRS duration of ≥0.10 seconds may be the best indication of the severity of the overdose.
